confidentUnsupported.evidence: Hedged with 'it's probably the battery pack itself' but then 'Once you swap it out, the issue should be resolved' - overconfident on outcome without excluding charger/contact or control faults

unjustifiedPart.evidence: 'I'd recommend buying an official replacement or a high-quality third-party one' - model never established (customer only said 'a V-something') and no swap test or Dyson diagnosis

rationale: The assistant reached the most plausible cause (a worn battery sagging under load, worse on Max) and explained it well, using the customer's own evidence about off-charger behaviour. However it never asked for the model label (SV11/V7), never asked about pulsing vs clean stop or the light pattern, and in turn 1 floated 'restricted airflow' despite the customer already stating filter and blockages were checked. It then told the customer to buy a battery (including third-party) without establishing the model or suggesting Dyson support/diagnosis, and closed with 'the issue should be resolved' when the ground truth says the cause cannot be confirmed remotely.
